references.text: Zipporah circumcises her son with a flint knife, illustrating the ancient practice of circumcision with stone tools also mentioned in Joshua 5:2
God commands Abraham regarding circumcision as a sign of the covenant, which is the basis for why the Israelites had to be circumcised again in Joshua 5:2
Circumcision was necessary to participate in the Passover meal, explaining why the Israelites had to be circumcised before celebrating Passover in the Promised Land
The continuation of the verse explaining that Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at Gibeath-Haaraloth
An explanation of why this second circumcision was necessary—the generation that left Egypt died in the wilderness without having circumcised their sons
Moses speaks about the circumcision of the heart, adding spiritual depth to the physical circumcision commanded in Joshua 5:2
A reference to an uncircumcised heart, showing the spiritual meaning behind the physical act of circumcision
Jeremiah speaks about circumcising the heart to the Lord, linking the physical action to spiritual renewal
